sections.title: 1 Executive Summary
paragraphs: J1P WS Development_Kit - Web Services Overview.docx

RESTRICTED This document contains Private and Proprietary information for use only by JAGGAER and its intended recipients and must not b e disclosed to unauthorized individuals without prior, express written consent from JAGGAER. Page 6 | 25

Jaggaer one platform (J1P) module provides the below list of options to integrate Jaggaer platform with customer ERP/ third party applications. Public APIs to Import /Update /Validate /Export data over REST protocol. Cloud Connectors to enrich the supplier information with market -recognized 3rd party Info Providers. Webhooks/connectors + “User aware” APIs to enable flexible PaaS Integrations developed by Partners to connect with customers and third -party applications . J1 IDM to enable Jaggaer as Identity Provider for third -party and customer applications with the abil ity to federate other IDPs (identity brokering) .

2 J1P Public API The Jaggaer one platform module (J 1P) offers REST web -services to import, update, export and validate data in to Jaggaer one platform. This document provides high level information about integrating customer ERP/ External system with Jaggaer one application.

paragraphs: J1P WS Development_Kit - Web Services Overview.docx

This chapter aims at describing some general features of J1P webservices, and in particular
- Guidelines for REST webservices
- The “grammar” defining query expression to filter resources
- The authentication methods
- Additional Security Measures and best practices

The list of available web -services is defined in the document “ J1P Web Services Library and Activation Request ” available on J 1P SharePoint portal. Additional details on each single web -service (e.g. specific resources, endpoints) are defined in the web -service development kit document of each single supported integration flow.

Please note that J1P REST APIs are designed to be consumed by the customer system and to transfer data among systems . Provided features, data visibility, authentication approach and other security measures such as anti -DOS filters, are then designed based on this assumption.

The list of available web -services and support ed protocols (is defined in the document “ J1P Web Services Library and Activation Request ” available on J 1P SharePoint portal. Additional details on REST APIs for specific webservices (e.g. specific resources, endpoints) are defined in the web - service deve lopment kit document of each single supported integration flow .

2.2 API Endpoints The APIS are exposed only on the J1P Public API URL on endpoints that are in the format <J1P_Public_API -URL> /j1p /api/public/< J1-MODULE>/<API -VERSION>/< RESOURCES -COLLECTION > e.g. https://prep -reg01.api.jaggaer.com/j1p/api/public/ja/v1/companyprofiles
Under the resource s collection are usually available

- The possibility to GET the resources given the ID or complex queries GET https://prep -reg01.api.jaggaer.com/j1p/api/public/ja/v1/companyprofiles /123456 or GET https://prep -reg01.api.jaggaer.com/j1p/api/public/ja/v1/companyprofiles /?flt=LASTMODTIME==20190801;TYPE==SELLER&start=1

Activation of API’s are managed over the J1P integration manager console and to activate the REST services for any tenant , log in to the console https://global.j1p.jaggaer.com/globalfe/ first and t hen select the region and choose the Public API option from the external integration submenu. Public APIs page allows you to search integrations or create new one, based on selected tenant. Every created integration has action submenu, marked with three do ts. For the activation of rest service, first choose Rest Configuration action, then on Rest Configuration page, use "Activate Service" button in top right corner of the page. Activation of rest service is done by selecting service by typing letters of ser vice name in search/or selecting from drop down menu, and then using "Activate Service" button in top right corner of this page and after successful activation return back to Rest Configuration page, which should show activated services in the list.
2.4 Query language

2.4.1 Introduction J1P allows to search REST collections by means of a query language based on the standard Feed Item Query Language (FIQL - https://tools.ietf.org/html/ draft -nottingham -atompub -fiql -00). The language has been extended to support additional operators and expressions required by J1P services A query expression (provided in query string parameter) can be composed by several comparison separated by semicolon, representing AND operator

Each comparison is composed by a
- selector: the field to be appl ied to the filter
- operator: the logical comparison operator
- the arguments to check the operator against. It can be single or multiple ones.

Allowed selectors and o perators depends on each single webservice and filter, will be then available in the specific development kit document . Argument can be a single value, or multiple values in parenthesis separated by comma. Value that doesn’t contain any reserved character or a white space can be unquoted, other arguments must be enclosed in single or double quotes. If you need to use both single and double quotes inside a quoted argument, then you must escape one of them using \ (backslash). If you want to use \ literally, then double it as \\. Backslash has a special meaning only inside a quoted argument, not in unquoted argument.

2.4.4 Query grammar specifications The following grammar specification is written in EBNF notation ( ISO 14977 ). query-expression = comparison, { ";" , comparison } selector = unreserved -str; comparison = selector, comparison -op, arguments; comparison -op = ( ( "=", { ALPHA } ) | "!" ), "="; arguments = ( "(", value, { "," , value }, ")" ) | value; value = unreserved -str | double -quoted | single -quoted;
unreserved -str = unreserved, { unreserved } single -quoted = "'", { ( escaped | all -chars - ( "'" | " \" ) ) }, "'"; double -quoted = '"', { ( escaped | all -chars - ( '"' | " \" ) ) }, '"';
reserved = '"' | "'" | "(" | ")" | ";" | "," | "=" | "!" | "~" | "<" | ">"; unreserved = all-chars - reserved - " "; escaped = "\", all -chars; all-chars = ? all unico de characters ?;

The REST interface support s the import of files into the Jaggaer platform together with data . Attachment’s import is supported through multipart POST ( multipart/form -data ). The post must contain:
- One parameter with a file representing the JSON payload (the same one used in plain data import); the name of the form parameter must be “data”
- One or more additional parameters for the files; each parameter must have as name the name given to the file in the JSON payload

E.g. if the JSON references a file named “doc1.pdf” there must be 2 parameters : “data” with the JSON, and “doc1.pdf” with the file . Refer to development kit documents for detailed examples.
Files can be also downloaded through the “ attachments ” REST API that is made available on each specific J1 module , as described in the related development kit document of each mo dule itse lf.
As per all J1P webservices REST APIs are protected through
- SSL encryption, i.e. they are ex posed on HTTPS

In addition to this all REST services are secured by means of additional measures requiring the API client to authenticate itself by means of a Bearer token . The authentication is always meant to identify the client component, not the end user, since the APIs are designed to transfer data between systems i.e. t he J1 platform and customer systems.
Below are described supported tokens and how the authentication process take s places

2.6.1 JWT – Json Web Token In order to authenticate itself against the API endpoint , user can use an opaque token that is provided by the J 1P authorization endpoint. Therefore the client components invoke the “Token” API providing some credentials and gets the bearer token to be used to call t he APIs. The access token can be retrieved by the client calling the “tokens” endpoint offered by J1P Public API and providing the credentials communicated at setup phase. In particu lar: URL <J1P_Public_API -URL>/auth/realms/J1p -integrations/protocol/openid -connect/token (e.g. https://prep -reg01.api.jaggaer.com /auth/realms/J1p -integrations/protocol/openid -connect/token ) Http Method POST Header Parameters Body Parameters client_id : client identifi er defined at setup phase client_secret : shared password defined at setup phase grant_type=client_credentials (fixed value)

This chapter introduces the PUSH integration services available in J1P for covered Jaggaer One modules.

Push services have been introduced to support real -time and near real -time process where it is required to send data from Jaggaer One to an external system and therefore an integration solution based on “CALL -ME” web -services ( only over REST ) based on a the PULL logic was not well -fitting since it requires the client component to “call” the web - services very frequently.

While in case of “call -me” services supporting the PULL logic, regardless of the data -flow direction, the J1P exposes a web-service to be invoked by a client component running at customer or partner side, in case of “push” services it is J1P that sends a message to the server component exposed by the partner/customer when an event occurs in Jaggaer One.

3.1.1 Pre-requisites To implement a “push” based integration the following pre -requisites need to be checked
- The required J1P dataflow must support the “push” based communication (please refer to the J1P Web Services Library and Activation request document)
- The customer/partner must be able to expose a service to receive the message sent by the J 1P and in the J 1P format (see 3.3-Message format ) and provide back a response in a timely manner
- The service must run on an URL exposed on the internet via HTTPS
3.2 Message exchange synchronisation

The message exchange between Jaggaer One platform and the external system (via the J1P ) can be synchronous or asynchronous. This depends mainly on the function al features available on the related JaggaerOne module and the required processes to be executed on the external system to provide a feedback (if they can be executed in real time or not).

3.2.1 Synchronous data exchange As soon as an event is generated by Jagga er One (e.g. a purchase order is approved in the workflow and an “export” robot is configured as next step) the J1P prepares the message and sends it to the configured endpoint.
The external system processes it immediately and provide as response the outco me of the process (e.g. if the purchase order is valid for the ERP).
JaggaerOne platform receives the response and operates accordingly based on available features and configuration.

3.2.2 Asynchronous data exchange When event is generated by Jaggaer One (e.g. a purchase order is approved in the workflow and a “validate” robot is configured as next step) the J1P prepares the message and sends it to the configured endpoint. The external system acknowledges J1 P it received the message and processes it on a later stage. Once the message has been processed the external system will call already available “call -me” web -services to inform Jaggaer One about the outcome of the process (e.g. if the purchase order is va lid for the ERP). When the external system processes the message, it could be required as well to consume other “call -me” web -services exposed by J1P to get additional data and/or files.
The web -service call will be processed according to the specific features available on involved the Jaggaer One module and related configuration Below diagram representing the synchronous exchange

• Header
- timestamp: the time the message was generated
- messageId: unique identified of the push message
- objectType: the type of the Jaggaer One object included in the push mes sage
- objectId: the ID of the Jaggaer One object included in the push message

code String Possible values are: ”OK” if the message has been correctly processed with positive res ult “KO” if the message has been processed but the external system identified some issue
description String (if present) description of the outcome of the operation (useful for possible required user actions)

To secure the communication between J1P and the external system is based on HTTPs only then the channel is encrypted The following additional security measures can be applied to allow the external system to authenticate the J1P
- HTTP Basic [segreto] : each HTTP message pushed by J1P to the external system contains username/password defined during the setup of the integration
- OAuth 2.0 authentication : each HTTP message pushed by J1P to the external system contains access token issued by the integration , valid for a fixed length of time .

5 J1 PaaS Integration

J1P provides configurable webhooks and public AP Is to enable flexible PaaS integration with external system developed by Jaggaer partners. Integration scenarios supported through PaaS integrations are
1) Data transfer from J1 to external Apps
2) Data transfer from external Apps to J1
3) UI driven integration PaaS integration or ‘Partner as a Service integration’ provide an option for the customers to independently manage the customer specific customizations over Jaggaer platform.

An ad -hoc UI/ application developed by Jaggaer partner for the Pa aS integration can be used to select /enrich the data or trigger an integration flow and can be used to visualize/confirm the integration flow execution results. Before a user redirect from the Jaggaer platform to PaaS custom UI page or vice versa, need to be authenticated internally and data transferred back and forth between J1 and the ad -hoc UI/application to be connected. For the authentication, there are two possible situations: users are authenticated by J1 APPS & users are authenticated by the custom er IDP. In both cases Jaggaer partner will be responsible for the development of ad - hoc UI/application and it need to deploy & run on an external infrastructure. Data exchange between Jaggaer & ad -hoc UI/application and the if required between customer ex ternal application & ad -hoc UI/application will be through a system -to-system channel using existing J1 APIs (to exchange data with Jaggaer) and customer system APIs (to exchange data with customer legacy systems). Custom ad -hoc UI/application should manag e authorization and data segregation to make sure the users are not allowed to execute /access any data or action not allowed for a specific user in J1 Apps. When the user redirected to the ad -hoc UI/application; the redirection includes needed parameters (e.g. the object id); and the ad-hoc UI/application authenticates the user with the IDP (SP initiated SSO), regardless if the IDP is the Jaggaer one or the Customer one and then ad -hoc UI/application interacts both with J1 and the customer legacy systems via API calls.

6.1 Internal users IDM Each J1p tenant can be federated with customer IDP to support access to J1p resource without any re -authentication step. In case the customer doesn’t have a IDP, J1P can enable a IDP service to federate, in addition to J1P module, also external application provided by the customer and/or Ipaas application dev eloped by Jaggaer partners . Username is the identification key to recognize the user Internal users IDM support only SP initiated scenario

6.2 Supplier users IDM Jaggaer also provide a centralized supplier IDM to allow supplier to access every single J1P tenant with the same credential Every time a supplier user needs to access a J1P resource, the J1 Supplier IDM will verify the supplier session and, if not valid, will ask the suppli er to authenticate himself Username will be the email Supplier IDM will also provide the possibility to support customer IDP federation, in addition to J1P supplier IDM one In case this option is applied, J1P supplier IDM will act as service provider towar ds the customer IDP by using a specific feature named Identity brokering If a supplier user access via customer IDP, access is restricted to the J1P tenant associated to the customer, via a J1P feature named Audience, that block the possibility for a suppl ier to access J1P tenant belonging to other customers
